verse.reading: You set your love on the leather bag with nine mouths as if each day were yesterday, my heart, and wandered, having seen the cruel vultures hop and hop, strike off the shirt of skin, bite, tear, peck, cut and eat.
verse.nuance: ஒருநாளைப் போலவே, as on one day, is loving the body as if it never changed. The last line is the metre's gallop put to work, seven verbs of the vultures' eating in one breath; சட்டை, the shirt, is the skin they tear off.

finding.claim: A microtubule-stabilising drug delayed isoflurane-induced unconsciousness in rats, consistent with but not proof of a microtubule role in consciousness.

verse.reading: As you simply look, drive the mind to the suzhumunai and see the breath there; subside, saying 'Mother, you are the Devi', and see; then come kaya-siddhi and yoga-siddhi; 'Um-ma' and 'Am-ma' are seen there; with one mind plant the mind at the suzhumunai; we have told all that was made by us; among the Nathars no one sings this.
verse.nuance: காயசித்தி, the perfected body, and யோகசித்தி are the two fruits claimed, and the means is the simplest the run offers: look, fix the mind, see the breath (கால்), address the Devi. உம்மாவும் அம்மாவும் may be two syllables (u-ma, a-ma) or the mother's two names; the text does not say. 'None of the Nathars sings this' claims the teaching goes beyond the Natha lineage.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.

verse.reading: A root from the underworld with arsenic added, with the goblin-drug joined and white-thorn ghee poured, a red vermilion ink that terrifies the whole world: by the drug she gave I burn like a coal, my Mother.
verse.nuance: The verse lists alchemical materials, பாடாணம், வேதாளம், செந்தூரம், as the Mother's drug, and its effect is the poet's burning. Whether the burning is the heat of the awakened power or the ruin of a failed preparation is open; both readings are traditional.

finding.claim: Case reports document severe poisoning, including cerebral edema, from Siddha capsules containing arsenic, mercury and lead thousands of times above safe limits.

verse.reading: From the navel by the way of the whirl to the middle of the crown, the red flame that leapt past the moon's light and the organs; becoming the bond in the bow's curve, the magic of the five elements; standing like a drop in 'kī', it said 'kīch mūch'.
verse.nuance: The clearest route in the chapter: navel, whirl, crown. கரணம், the organs, are the inner instruments the flame passes. கிந்து is probably விந்து (bindu). கீச்சுமூச்சு is onomatopoeia for a squeak and a breath, with மூச்சு the breath itself; the verse ends in the body's own noise.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.

verse.reading: Making the sky a bow and the five letters an arrow, mounting the chariot of mantra to hunt the deer, in the grove where the moon and sun have gone, will I not come and play and look with a glad mind, my Mother?
verse.nuance: The deer hunt is the chase of the restless mind (மான் as deer and as the mind). Sun and moon are the two breaths in Siddhar cipher; the grove where they have gone is where the two channels end and the central one opens. The five letters are the Siva mantra.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: When will I leave the two country legs, go through the middle leg, and sit within the two goat legs?
verse.nuance: Wholly in cipher. நாட்டுக்கால் (the two legs planted in the country), நடுவுக்கால் (the middle leg) and ஆட்டுக்கால் (the two goat legs) are read by the tradition as ida and pingala, the sushumna, and a pair at the upper end (the two brows or two eyes, the 'moving' pair); 96 says the first two plainly. The plain words give a man stepping between legs of unlike kinds, which is not a sentence, so the cipher is the only reading.

finding.claim: Most healthy adults show a nasal cycle in which airflow alternates between the left and right nostril over hours, driven by autonomic congestion of the nasal lining.

verse.reading: As men of means are known by their acts, warriors on the battlefield and the clear-minded by their faces, so those who have grace are to be recognised by their austerity, their nature, their grace and love, and even by their obscure words.
verse.nuance: இருளுறு சொல், words wrapped in darkness, is the mark the stanza ends on: the speech of the graced is dark to others, a near description of the Siddhars' own cipher. The Kural's மறைமொழி (28) makes the same point for the great.

finding.claim: Loving-kindness and compassion meditation improve self-reported wellbeing and reduce distress in small to moderate degree.

verse.reading: Praise the dense Substance that is formless and formed, that is the twilight and the end, the light and the Agama, the Lady and the guru and the living soul, and dance.
verse.nuance: அருவாயும் உருவாயும் is the Saiva pair of formless and formed. அந்தி may be twilight (the junction, as the yogis' time) or a corruption of அந்தம் doubled with the next word. திரு here could be Lakshmi, Shakti or simply the holy; the stanza's point is that one Substance is all these.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: They wander saying 'muppu', but they do not see the way that muppu came to be; if one turns back and says 'that is the flower', it becomes attainment, and dance.
verse.nuance: முப்பு is the Siddhars' three-salt preparation, the catalyst of their alchemy, whose identity is itself a secret of the tradition. The stanza puns on பூ: முப்பூ as three flowers and அப்பூ, 'that flower', as something turned back toward (மறித்தால்), which in the kummi's cipher is the breath turned inward; the plain and the coded readings both stand.

finding.claim: Mercury can be turned into gold only by nuclear reactions such as neutron bombardment of mercury isotopes, never by chemical or alchemical processing.

verse.reading: Not knowing the alchemy, saying 'we practise rasavaadham', they put mercury and sulphur in the crucible; will gold grow from it, girl?
verse.nuance: சூதம் (mercury) and கெந்தி (sulphur) are the base pair of Siddha alchemy; the stanza does not deny transmutation, it denies that heating the two without the knowledge (வாதம்) yields it. The claim is historical, that practitioners of the time did exactly this.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: The world is imagination, an expanse produced by the inner faculties, a dream, an Indra's net; if on that day it appears so, that is favourable to the subtle.
verse.nuance: அந்தக்கரணம், the inner faculties (mind, intellect, ego, will), are made the producers of the world, which is Vedanta's idealism; இந்த்ரசாலம் is the conjuror's show. The last line is obscure: perhaps that once the world has appeared as dream, the subtle is in reach. 2291 returns to the faculties and says their play cannot be pushed away.

finding.claim: Calculated decoherence times for neural quantum states are far shorter than neural processing times, a central objection to quantum-brain theories.

verse.reading: If you go about cherishing desire for women, there is no way left to set your desire on heaven, stony mind.
verse.nuance: The second of three desires named in 1790 to 1793: land (rule), women and gold, the stock triad of the Siddhars. விண்ணாசை, desire for the sky, is the one desire that is allowed.

finding.claim: Nasal breathing entrains oscillations in olfactory and limbic brain areas and improves memory and fear recognition timed to inhalation, an effect absent with mouth breathing.

verse.reading: If you go about cherishing desire for women, there is no way left to set your desire on heaven, stony mind.
verse.nuance: The second of three desires named in 1790 to 1793: land (rule), women and gold, the stock triad of the Siddhars. விண்ணாசை, desire for the sky, is the one desire that is allowed.

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

verse.reading: Was it not by burning the ghost's nature that we saw the Brahma-state? Passing beyond Brahma's seat we took our place in the sushumna; not roaming like a dog, we stayed in tapas, having subdued the ego well and with dignity.
verse.nuance: பிரமநிலை and பிரமபதி may be Brahman (the Supreme state) or Brahma the creator, whose seat in the yogic map is a lower centre; on the second reading the stanza is coded, the breath passing Brahma's centre and entering the central channel. நல்லதொரு ஆங்காரம், a 'good' ego that is subdued, is odd; the sense may be that even the good self-regard is held down.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of small randomised trials finds alternate-nostril breathing lowers blood pressure modestly, with high heterogeneity between studies.

verse.reading: Thinking on the letter with the curl, setting it at the mouth of speech, passing beyond pain and pleasure, going through the channel they speak of, raising the fire of the firm akshara, and crossing the six lotuses, in the space beyond ...
verse.nuance: The sentence runs on into 1194. சுழித்ததோர் எழுத்து, the letter with a curl, is taken by tradition as Om (or its ஓ); அக்கிரம் may be அக்ஷரம், the letter, or அக்ர, the tip or crown; the fire raised and the six lotuses crossed are the serpent power and the six supports in the yogic body. The verse describes an ascent through the central channel in the Siddhars' usual terms without naming them.

finding.claim: Claims that breathing through one nostril selectively activates the opposite brain hemisphere or shifts sympathetic versus parasympathetic tone rest on small, inconsistent studies.

verse.reading: The space that deluded you within as a circle; within the eight-fold figure, the containing and the subsiding; within the moving wheel that is eight and eight and eight, what can be reached rose, once we had known our Lord.
verse.nuance: அட்டவக்கரம் may be the eight-letter mantra or an eight-cornered figure; எட்டும் எட்டும் எட்டும் (twenty-four) may count tattvas or petals. எட்டலாம் puns on எட்டு, eight, and எட்டல், reaching. The plain sense is that the body's wheel becomes legible after knowing the Lord, not before.

finding.claim: Emotion and the sense of self may arise as predictions about the body's internal state, extending predictive processing to interoception.

verse.reading: Since the inner meaning of the Agamas is the undivided root, you, the Supreme, are held without thirst or enjoyment; setting the one foot, within the five letters that make known, it stood as the one enjoyment: Sivayam.
verse.nuance: அகண்டமூலம், the undivided root, is the claim: the Agamas reduce to one thing, and that thing is the five letters. ஏகபாதம் (one foot) and ஏகபோகம் (one enjoyment) are unexplained; tradition would take the foot as the Lord's single step or the one syllable, and the enjoyment as union.

finding.claim: Meta-analysis of morphometric studies reports modest structural brain differences in meditators across about eight regions, though small samples and publication bias are concerns.

verse.reading: Not knowing the alchemy, saying 'we practise rasavaadham', they put mercury and sulphur in the crucible; will gold grow from it, girl?
verse.nuance: சூதம் (mercury) and கெந்தி (sulphur) are the base pair of Siddha alchemy; the stanza does not deny transmutation, it denies that heating the two without the knowledge (வாதம்) yields it. The claim is historical, that practitioners of the time did exactly this.

finding.claim: Mouse studies reported that sleep increases clearance of brain waste through the glymphatic system, but a 2024 study found clearance fell during sleep, so the claim is disputed.

verse.reading: Om: listen, pupil of ruined mind; in the world a man's years are a hundred; is it not twenty-one thousand six hundred breaths in a day? Because they went, going out with the breath, the days diminished and were gone; if they do not go out, there is no going; when a man thinks one thing, the god thinks it too; are not fates only what one has thought?
verse.nuance: The breath-count of 21,600 a day is the standard figure of the hatha texts (fifteen a minute), and the verse's arithmetic is the Siddhar theory of life: a life is a fixed number of breaths, so the breath held is life saved. The last two lines go further and make விதி (fate) the product of one's own thought, with the god only concurring.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: The poet says he does not know the measure of you who stood as ida and pingala and as the suzhumunai that rose, as body and as life.
verse.nuance: The three channels are named outright and the Lord is identified with them, not placed in them; எழுந்த சுழுமுனை, the whirl-channel that rose, is the middle channel the Siddhars prize, called risen because the breath rises in it. உளவு, the measure or secret, is what is unknown.

finding.claim: Most healthy adults show a nasal cycle in which airflow alternates between the left and right nostril over hours, driven by autonomic congestion of the nasal lining.

verse.reading: Pingala is where the rechaka is; placing the growing puraka in the left, so as to hold it as kumbhaka in Nandi: is this not the Siva-gaze, jnana girl?
verse.nuance: Breath in by the left channel (இடம், idai), out by pingalai on the right, held 'in Nandi', the place of the guru at the brow of 2572. சிவநாட்டம், the Siva-gaze, makes the breath-hold and the fixed look one act.

finding.claim: Most healthy adults show a nasal cycle in which airflow alternates between the left and right nostril over hours, driven by autonomic congestion of the nasal lining.

verse.reading: He is the pearl's light within the shell; to those who lack the gaze of consciousness he is the rare substance that stays unseen, like light in water.
verse.nuance: Both images are of a light that is present but not seen unless one looks rightly; சின்மய நோக்கு, the gaze of consciousness, is what 611 says the Lord gave her.

finding.claim: Meditators report a wide range of challenging experiences, including perceived lights, altered self-sense, fear and lasting distress, some needing support.

verse.reading: The bellows is there, the smith is there, the golden light is there; if you can think with a mind set right and blow so that it shines, the great pillar will blaze and spread as a mass of flame, and nothing remains but the dancing light and you.
verse.nuance: The smithy is the body: the bellows the breath, the smith the practitioner or the Lord, the pillar the spine or the flame-linga. The verse answers 1149's 'if you can blow' with what the blowing is for, and its end is not gold but a light that dances (நிருத்தமான சோதி) and a 'you' left standing with it.

finding.claim: Slow controlled breathing is associated with greater parasympathetic activity, more alpha power and lower arousal and anxiety, though most trials are small.

verse.reading: Calling the waking oneself, and beyond it the one who owns it: the wise will name him Virat; know it, girl of knowledge.
verse.nuance: விராட்டன் (Virat) is the cosmic counterpart of Visva: the Lord identified with the gross universe in its 'waking'. காமர் is probably a misprint for the wise or the learned.

finding.claim: An underground radiation experiment ruled out the simplest parameter-free version of the gravity-related collapse model that Orch-OR depends on.

verse.reading: When sleep comes and forgets the books recited, the learning understood, wife, children and kin, where did they go and hide, or did they stand become everywhere? Tell me, Lord, the mystery of their hiding in the light.
verse.nuance: Sleep is used as a test: whatever vanishes nightly, learning and family alike, cannot be what one is. The last line offers two answers in the form of a question, that they hid somewhere or that they became everything, and leaves both open. 1172 repeats the stanza with mantras and Agamas in place of books.

finding.claim: Mouse studies reported that sleep increases clearance of brain waste through the glymphatic system, but a 2024 study found clearance fell during sleep, so the claim is disputed.

verse.reading: If the mad monkey of the mind, seized too by a frenzied ghost, starts its revels, when one makes the medicine to subdue it the horse can then be ridden.
verse.nuance: மனக்குரங்கு is the standard image of the restless mind; the ghost that possesses it is the family of 2618 to 2620. The medicine is named in 2625 as the silent vaasi, and in 2626 as knowledge and dispassion.

finding.claim: People's minds wander nearly half their waking time, and they report being less happy while wandering than while focused.

verse.reading: The pedestal of the linga in the body, the three letters of the unspoken mantra, the conch and the discus, all the sky; the yogis who have taken their share there, the five supreme gates and the lion-roar sound: nothing is other than Sivayam.
verse.nuance: The gloss gives அசவை as the ajapa mantra, the unrecited syllables of the breath (in tradition ஹம்ஸ or சோகம்), here counted as three letters. Conch and discus are Vishnu's, so the stanza claims the Vaishnava emblems for Sivayam too. பரம வாசல் அஞ்சு, the five supreme gates, is not fixed, perhaps the five senses or five centres. Near-repeat of 1138.

finding.claim: Reciting a rosary prayer or a yoga mantra slows breathing to about six a minute and raises baroreflex sensitivity, linking repetitive recitation to the slow-breath physiology.

verse.reading: If you go about cherishing desire for women, there is no way left to set your desire on heaven, stony mind.
verse.nuance: The second of three desires named in 1790 to 1793: land (rule), women and gold, the stock triad of the Siddhars. விண்ணாசை, desire for the sky, is the one desire that is allowed.

finding.claim: A single 25 mg dose of psilocybin with psychological support reduced treatment-resistant depression scores at three weeks more than 1 mg, with adverse events in both arms.

verse.reading: Doing the vaasi exactly by rechaka, puraka and kumbhaka is also desire; reach the non-dual Brahman that is the sky-going state and dance the kummi.
verse.nuance: This opens the litany of ஆசையடி, 'that too is desire'. Breath-counting is placed among the observances to be outgrown, although the same kummi taught the vaasi at the root triangle (2593, 2615). One reading is that the measured pranayama of the manuals is the desire, and the vaasi proper is the khechara Brahman itself; another is that at this point the song leaves practice for Vedanta. கேசரம் is the 'moving in space' that 2642 promised the inner alchemy.

finding.claim: Breathing voluntarily at about six breaths a minute raises vagally mediated heart-rate variability during practice, right after one session and after multi-session training.

verse.reading: Tearing the silk, taking out the thick needle with care, rolling it up tight and giving it into the hands of my wife with her swarming hair; was it so that all the desire of this heavy maya-woman, who held me bound, should leave and part from me that Siva turned back like this?
verse.nuance: The verse belongs to the story of Pattinathar's renunciation, in which a needle sent to him in a box carried the message that not even an eyeless needle goes with one at death; the details of silk and rolling cannot be recovered from the verse alone. கனமாயக்காரி, the heavy sorceress, is the wife as maya; சிவன் மீண்டது, Siva turning back or returning, is the poet's name for what happened to him.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: The desire for mantras says 'I will not forget'; the desire for beauty says 'I will not renounce'.
verse.nuance: சுந்தரம் may be the beauty of others or the poet's own adornment; the verse does not say which. Mantras follow siddhis (440) as a second item of religious craving.

finding.claim: People adapt to most gains and losses so that happiness drifts back toward a personal set point, though not fully for every life event.

tamil: பாலை இறக்கி உண்டு பசி ஒழிவது எக்காலம்?
verse.reading: When will I leave the root fire, kindle it in the hall of the moon, bring down the milk, drink it and end hunger?
verse.nuance: A cipher verse: மூலநெருப்பு is the fire at the base (kundalini), நிலா மண்டபம் the moon-hall at the crown, and பால் the nectar the tradition says drips from the moon when the fire reaches it; the hunger ended is bodily (the yogi who no longer needs food) and the soul's. Plainly it is a kitchen scene, fire moved and milk warmed, and the cipher is why it is not one.

finding.claim: People across cultures locate distinct emotions in consistent regions of the body, suggesting feelings are partly constructed from bodily sensation.

verse.reading: The thought takes the body, a bubble on water, for permanent; the desire that rises above all says 'I will not perish'.
verse.nuance: நீர்க்குமிழி, the water bubble, is the Naladiyar's image for the body (27). ஆர்க்கும் உயர் ஆசை may be the desire higher than all others or the desire that rises in everyone; it closes the run of speaking desires.

finding.claim: In two combined randomised trials, eight weeks of mindfulness training produced no structural brain changes compared with active and waitlist controls.

verse.reading: After it has dried, take it, son, and set it devotedly in a kasaputa fire; let it cool, and when you take it out it is a sindhuram of the colour of the dawn sun; smear an atom of it on every drug and set them in the puta: the nine metals yield, and the whole art called vedai is in your hands.
verse.nuance: செந்தூரம் is the red calcined product of Siddha chemistry; நவலோகம் the nine metals; the claim is a universal agent that transmutes. நீருமடா may mean the metals turn to liquid or lose their nature. Read as history of a claim, not as a method.

finding.claim: A typical human body holds roughly as many bacterial cells as human cells, so the body is in large part a community of other organisms.

verse.reading: The beginningless mantra that is five and three and is not reached: if you think of it in your heart and recite it until you take its form, even a hundred crore of the five great sins fly off like cotton, so the four Vedas declare.
verse.nuance: அஞ்சும் மூணும் எட்டாதாய் puns on எட்டு: five and three make eight, and the mantra is 'unreachable'. Tradition reads the eight as the five letters with the three of Om, or as an eight-syllable mantra. நீருருச் செபிப்பீரேல் may be 'recite till you become it' or 'recite (while) you are water' (that is, at bathing). Compare 1022, which again joins five and three in one letter.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.

verse.reading: Desire for women will not do; if that delusion takes hold it does not go even a little; do not die in fear at Yama's hand; do not burn in the fire called wicked desire-bonds.
verse.nuance: ஆசாபாசம், desire-bond, is a compound the Siddhars favour, treating craving and the bond it makes as one thing; it is a fire here where 2276 made it poison.

finding.claim: The brain's dopamine 'wanting' system can drive craving independently of 'liking', so addictive desire can grow while pleasure does not.

verse.reading: We will take the eight nagas in our hands and make them dance, we will show Indra's world right here, we will bind and release the snake that no binding holds; spit out your fierce poison and dance.
verse.nuance: The Siddhar's boast begins. The eight nagas (Ananta, Vasuki, Takshaka, Karkotaka, Padma, Mahapadma, Shankhapala, Kulika) are named in 2014 and 2015; the uncontrollable snake made to spit its poison is on the coded reading the mind or the kundalini emptied of its venom. The stanza presents a power, not a procedure.

finding.claim: Reported evidence for precognition and other psychic powers failed to replicate and exposed weaknesses in standard statistical practice.

verse.reading: The poet, whose love and thought go only to the quarrelsome, sinful women whose eyes run to their ears and who play with the sore at their hips, and who has not been granted the fortune of wearing the Lord's two lotus feet, describes his own body as a wilderness where the five thieves raid, a chest of urine and excrement, a casket of the two deeds, a hamlet where wind, bile and phlegm lodge, a bloody frame of filthy skin, a stinking pot, a torn rag of four cubits and nine, a garden of bitter gourd, a mound in the great cremation ground, a top spinning on the rope of desire, a ship of ceaseless disease, a changing illusion, a cage of death, a bellows for rice, a kite flying in the wind, a log that fate's Dharma cuts, a shirt the four-faced tailor stitches, a feast thrown to the pyre, a dry leaf shrivelling in the fire of lust, a tuber worms dig, a forked branch up which the shoot of sin climbs, a lump that walks as a bridegroom and ends lying as a corpse, a burden the town will not let lie, a heap of pulai flowers against the wind, frost before the morning sun, a rainbow moving in the sky, the passing shadow of a thundering cloud, a bubble on water, writing on water, a sight seen in sleep's dream, and, worse than all of these, a stain of maya; and says enough, enough, Lord, enough: show the dance of bliss while the daughter of the mountain cries 'live', take me and rule me, for that is the beauty of your grace.
verse.nuance: The names fall into kinds: the body as a container of waste, as a thing moved by what is not itself (the top on the rope of desire, the kite in the wind, the puppet of 240), as a thing already prepared for death (the log Dharma cuts, the shirt Brahma sews, the feast for the fire), and as the stock brief things, which the poet caps by saying the body is worse than a bubble or a dream because it is a மாயக் களங்கம், a stain made of maya. சதுர்முகப் பாணன், the four-faced tailor, is Brahma stitching the body; விதிவழித் தருமன் is Yama as Dharma. நான்முழத் தொன்பது பீற்றத் துண்டம் is obscure: a torn cloth four cubits long with nine (holes), or nine torn pieces of four cubits. ஊரிற் கிடக்க ஒட்டா உபாதி uses the Siddhanta word உபாதி loosely for the corpse the town hurries out. The petition at the end is brief, and the grace asked for is to be ruled (ஆண்டுகொண்டருள்), not to be released.

finding.claim: People across cultures locate distinct emotions in consistent regions of the body, suggesting feelings are partly constructed from bodily sensation.

verse.reading: The kundalini-breath is the letter A; at the throat of the nape is the next letter; if you place the letter M at the whirl, is this not Siva-yoga, jnana girl?
verse.nuance: The text has அகாரம் twice; the second, at the throat, must be உகாரம் (U), giving A, U and M of Om at the root, the throat and the whirl at the crown. குண்டலி வாசி joins the coiled power to the breath, as the Siddhars do: raising the breath is raising kundalini.

finding.claim: About one in five Ayurvedic products bought online in the US contained detectable lead, mercury or arsenic, including rasa shastra metal preparations.

verse.reading: The poet knew the mantra, reached and firmly knew the circle of the Omkara, realised the Indra seat, and seeing what the state of silence is, his mind took on goodness.
verse.nuance: ஓங்கார வட்டம், the circle of Om, may be a drawn yantra or the round of the syllable's parts. இந்திர பீடம், the Indra seat, is unexplained: perhaps the seat of the senses (இந்திரியம்), perhaps a centre named for Indra as the east. எட்டி அறிந்தேன் is 'reached and knew', not 'knew the eight'.

finding.claim: Silent repetition of a single word reduces activity widely across the cortex, including default-mode regions, compared with rest.
